questions.text: How many phases comprise the Regular Design Services under SPP 202?

rationale.a: 4 phases is too few. SPP 202 has a more detailed phasing structure.
rationale.b: 5 phases is incorrect. SPP 202 specifies 6 distinct phases.
rationale.c: Correct. SPP 202 defines 6 phases: (1) Schematic Design, (2) Design Development, (3) Contract Documents, (4) Bidding/Negotiation, (5) Construction, and (6) Post-Construction.
rationale.d: 7 phases is too many. The SPP 202 structure has exactly 6 phases.
rationale.correct: Regular Design Services under SPP 202 consist of 6 phases: Schematic Design, Design Development, Contract Documents, Bidding/Negotiation, Construction Phase Services, and Post-Construction Phase Services.
rationale.takeaway: SPP 202 has 6 phases: SD, DD, CD, Bidding, Construction, Post-Construction.

questions.text: Under SPP 202, when the Contract Documents Phase represents 90% of the total work, how much of the design fee is the architect entitled to at that point?

rationale.a: 75% is incorrect. The fee entitlement corresponds proportionally to the work completed.
rationale.b: 80% is incorrect. SPP 202 ties fee entitlement to the percentage of work completed.
rationale.c: 85% is incorrect. The principle under SPP 202 is direct proportionality.
rationale.d: Correct. When the Contract Documents phase represents 90% of the total architectural work, the architect is entitled to 90% of the total design fee at that milestone.
rationale.correct: Under SPP 202, fee entitlement is proportional to work completed. Since the Contract Documents phase represents 90% of the total architectural work, the architect is entitled to 90% of the total design fee upon completion of this phase.
rationale.takeaway: Contract Documents = 90% of work = 90% of fee entitlement.

questions.text: What is the minimum design fee percentage for Group 4 (Residences) under SPP 202?

rationale.a: 7% applies to simpler building groups, not residences which require more detailed design.
rationale.b: 8% is incorrect for Group 4. Residences command a higher fee due to their design complexity and customization.
rationale.c: Correct. Group 4 (Residences) has a minimum design fee of 10% of PCC, reflecting the intensive, personalized design attention residences require.
rationale.d: 12% is incorrect for Group 4. While some specialized buildings may reach this rate, residences are at 10%.
rationale.correct: Group 4 (Residences) under SPP 202 carries a minimum design fee of 10% of PCC. Residences command a higher percentage than commercial buildings because of the individualized design, multiple custom details, and intensive client interaction required.

questions.text: Under SPP 202, what is the fee rate for Group 9 (Alterations, Renovations, and Additions)?

options.text: Same rate as the applicable Group 1-5 category

rationale.a: The same rate is insufficient because alterations involve additional complexity of working within existing structures.
rationale.b: 125% is incorrect. The premium for alteration work is higher than 25% above base rate.
rationale.c: Correct. Group 9 (Alterations) fee is 150% of the applicable Group 1-5 rate, reflecting the added complexity of working within existing buildings.
rationale.d: 200% is too high. While alterations are complex, the SPP sets the premium at 150%, not double.
rationale.correct: Group 9 (Alterations, Renovations, and Additions) carries a fee of 150% of the applicable Group 1-5 rate. The 50% premium recognizes the additional complexity of surveying existing conditions, working around occupied spaces, and integrating new work with old.
rationale.takeaway: Group 9 (Alterations) = 150% of the applicable Group 1-5 rate.

questions.text: What is the minimum fee percentage for Group 8 (Buildings Requiring Extensive Detail) under SPP 202?

rationale.b: 12% is incorrect. Group 8 buildings requiring extensive detail have a higher fee rate.
rationale.c: Correct. Group 8 (Buildings Requiring Extensive Detail) has a minimum fee of 15% of PCC, the highest standard group rate in SPP 202.
rationale.d: 18% exceeds the SPP 202 specification for Group 8. While negotiable, the minimum is 15%.
rationale.correct: Group 8 (Buildings Requiring Extensive Detail) carries the highest standard group rate at 15% of PCC. This applies to buildings like museums, theaters, and laboratories that require exceptionally detailed and specialized architectural work.
rationale.takeaway: Group 8 (Extensive Detail buildings) = 15% of PCC — highest group rate.

questions.text: How many sets of construction drawings are required for a building permit application under SPP 202?

rationale.a: 5 sets is insufficient for a building permit application under SPP 202.
rationale.b: 6 sets is incorrect. SPP 202 specifies a higher number.
rationale.c: Correct. SPP 202 requires 7 sets of construction drawings for a building permit application.
rationale.d: 8 sets exceeds the SPP 202 requirement for building permit drawings.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 requires the architect to prepare 7 sets of construction drawings for building permit application. These sets are distributed among various reviewing agencies and the owner.
rationale.takeaway: Building permit requires 7 sets of construction drawings.

questions.text: Under SPP 202, through whom must the Owner communicate instructions to the contractor?

rationale.a: Direct owner-to-contractor communication bypasses the architect's authority and is not permitted under SPP 202.
rationale.b: The project manager route applies under SPP 206 (CAS), not as the standard under SPP 202.
rationale.c: Correct. Under SPP 202, all Owner instructions to the contractor must flow through the Architect, preserving the architect's authority over design intent and construction quality.
rationale.d: The construction manager route applies under SPP 204-B, not as the standard under SPP 202.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 establishes that all Owner orders and instructions to the contractor must flow through the Architect. This ensures the architect maintains authority over design intent, construction quality, and contract administration.
rationale.takeaway: Owner orders to contractor must flow through the Architect under SPP 202.

questions.text: Under SPP 202, what radial distance from the architect's office triggers per diem travel compensation?

rationale.a: 25 km is too short. The SPP 202 threshold allows for reasonable local travel without additional compensation.
rationale.b: Correct. SPP 202 specifies that per diem travel compensation is triggered when the project site exceeds 50 km radial distance from the architect's principal office.
rationale.c: 75 km is incorrect. The threshold is lower at 50 km.
rationale.d: 100 km is the reimbursable travel threshold under SPP 201 for pre-design services, not the per diem trigger under SPP 202.
rationale.correct: Under SPP 202, per diem travel compensation is triggered when the project site is beyond 50 km radial distance from the architect's principal office. This is distinct from the 100 km threshold in SPP 201 for reimbursable pre-design travel.
rationale.takeaway: SPP 202 per diem travel threshold = 50 km (vs. SPP 201 reimbursable = 100 km).

questions.text: Under SPP 202, what happens to the architect's fee if construction is suspended for more than 6 months?

options.text: The fee remains unchanged, regardless of the duration of the suspension, ensuring financial stability for the architect
The fee is increased by 25%, reflecting the additional administrative burden and potential inflationary impacts
The fee is doubled for the remaining work
The contract is automatically terminated, requiring renegotiation if the project resumes

rationale.a: Unchanged fees do not compensate the architect for the disruption and carrying costs of a prolonged suspension.
rationale.b: A 25% increase is insufficient under SPP 202 for suspensions exceeding 6 months.
rationale.c: Correct. Under SPP 202, if construction is suspended for more than 6 months, the architect's fee for the remaining work is doubled to compensate for the disruption, remobilization, and extended engagement period.
rationale.d: Automatic termination is not specified. The contract continues but with adjusted compensation.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 provides that when construction is suspended for more than 6 months, the architect's fee for the remaining work is doubled. This compensates for the disruption to the architect's practice, the need to remobilize, and the extended engagement period.
rationale.takeaway: Construction suspension > 6 months = architect's remaining fee is doubled.

questions.text: Under SPP 202, is the architect required to provide continuous 8-hour on-site supervision during construction?

options.text: Yes, the architect must be present for 8 hours daily, ensuring all work complies with the design
No, SPP 202 requires only periodic site visits, not continuous supervision
Yes, but only during critical construction phases, such as foundation and structural work
No, supervision is optional under SPP 202, allowing flexibility in project management

rationale.a: Continuous 8-hour supervision is NOT required under SPP 202. This is the scope of SPP 204-A (Fulltime Supervision).
rationale.b: Correct. SPP 202 requires only periodic site visits during construction, not continuous 8-hour daily supervision. Full-time supervision is a separate service under SPP 204-A.
rationale.c: Even during critical phases, SPP 202 does not mandate continuous presence. That level of supervision falls under SPP 204-A.
rationale.d: Supervision is not optional — periodic visits ARE required under SPP 202. But continuous 8-hour supervision is not.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 requires periodic site visits during construction, not continuous 8-hour supervision. Full-time construction supervision (daily 8-hour presence) is a separate, additional service covered under SPP 204-A and compensated separately.
rationale.takeaway: SPP 202 = periodic visits only. Continuous 8-hour supervision = SPP 204-A (separate fee).
